comparator.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh 31 October 2026 inspection of the public OSIRIS examination programme ECTRIE/FEWBA26ECTRI establishes the 2026 entrant pathway: 60+60+60 EC. This controls over historical transition tables, the prior-year ESE/EFR guide and the public 2027–2028 preview. Econometrics is selected under the neutral broad-identity rule, independently of UCR fit. The 20-EC major is Advanced Econometrics4, one restricted methods course4 (Quantitative Methods for Data Science selected) and one seminar12 (Seminar in Forecasting selected). Career Skills2 is split into mandatory Your Future Career1 and an offered Job Market Skills1 choice. Genuine minor12 and remaining electives12 are preserved. Thesis10 is a compulsory award requirement under OER Arts10–12; the catalogue retains an older administrative thesis registration record, which is not treated as a new offered2026 course or an omitted requirement. Programme-specific guidance is non-credit. Current course descriptions confirm the foundations and prerequisite chain; Ethics precedes the major seminar, which precedes the individual major-linked thesis. All years1–2 completed before the seminar.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Operations research, optimisation and decision models
Research practice, academic skills and ethics
questions: How can real economic and business problems be translated into mathematical models and optimised?
How can data be used to estimate, forecast and support decisions under uncertainty?

trace: Develops financial and management accounting, financial-statement analysis, costing, budgeting and investment appraisal through NPV, IRR and cost-of-capital analysis. This supplies actual corporate-finance decision tools as well as business context, without becoming specialist financial econometrics.
examines how AI changes business and economic decision-making, supplying an application context for data-science methods

Studies bonds, shares, derivatives, interest rates and banking institutions, then applies financial and monetary analysis in simulated-bank management (loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk) and a small research project. This supplies substantive financial decisions and institutional content without specialist financial econometrics.
provides the introductory microeconomic and macroeconomic framework needed for quantitative economic applications
develops macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, policy, crises and international trade using economic data
develops advanced microeconomic analysis of uncertainty, strategic behaviour, market structure, equilibrium and efficiency
uses theoretical models and empirical evidence to analyse market failure, taxation, redistribution and public policy
directly develops econometric estimation, testing, causal analysis, prediction and Monte Carlo simulation in Stata
develops evidence-based analysis of economic decision-making, biases and behavioural choice
provides entrepreneurial and business-planning context for the finance direction; it does not contribute specialist quantitative-finance methods
provides foundational research design, statistics and empirical-analysis skills for later econometric work
adds explicit ethical analysis of algorithmic systems, including fairness, accountability, privacy and responsibility

Studies probability and Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability, bandits and multi-agent interaction. It contributes substantive decisions under uncertainty and discrete temporal modelling, not a general resource-planning or logistics course.

Develops propositional and predicate logic, sets, functions, proof, induction and recursion, followed by formal modelling of games without chance and winning strategies. It supports mathematical reasoning; a full combinatorics, graph or optimisation syllabus is not assumed.
develops search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation methods in discrete and continuous environments
develops algorithmic learning and sequential decision-making through reinforcement-learning models

Develops C++ classes, inheritance, polymorphism and memory management, Haskell functional programming, design, debugging, testing and version control. It adds substantive software construction to the computational direction.
develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational modelling

Develops advanced arithmetic and matrix algorithms, hashing, greedy and dynamic programming, and network flows, with analysis and experimental evaluation. These provide actual discrete algorithmic solution methods, without claiming a complete operations-research sequence.
develops foundational data cleaning, visualisation and analysis through applied research projects
develops predictive modelling through regression, classification, resampling, tree methods and clustering
adds advanced neural-network modelling and Python implementation to the Data Science for Econometrics direction
provides the programming foundation in Python, computational problem-solving and basic discrete mathematics

Develops single-variable limits, differentiation, optimisation, series, integration and differential equations, with Mathematica and a dynamic-model project. Linear algebra is supplied separately by DISMATH211.
develops matrix methods, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems of linear equations

Develops numerical root finding, linear systems, approximation, integration and differential-equation solution, with computational analysis of error and convergence. It is not claimed as a dedicated optimisation course.
extends calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations for quantitative modelling
Develops relational data modelling, SQL, normalisation, querying, transactions and access control. These organise data for later analysis; no particular economic or finance dataset is assumed.
develops probability theory, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation as a mathematical-statistics foundation

Develops moral philosophy through close reading, comparison and evaluation of ethical arguments and independent essays. It supplies ethical-theory foundations; econometric research integrity and adviser–client knowledge asymmetry are not assumed topics.
provides multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis and related inference methods useful for complex empirical data

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, econometrics & optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around economics, econometrics and optimisation, supported by mathematics, statistics, programming, algorithms and data analysis; the label avoids presenting UCR as offering the comparator's full specialist econometrics sequence.
alternatives.concept: A quantitative response to Econometrics and Operations Research built around mathematics, statistics, econometrics, economics, programming, algorithms and optimisation.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.

alternatives.label: Econometrics, data science & predictive modelling
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains the econometric and economic core but adds software development, neural networks, AI ethics and AI/business applications, making data science and predictive modelling a visible organising strand rather than calling the whole programme simply Econometrics.
alternatives.concept: A computational economic-data direction combining econometrics with programming, software development, machine learning, neural networks, algorithms and quantitative economic applications.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest-match curriculum, this route replaces accounting/corporate finance, public economics, numerical methods and general ethics with database management, software development, neural networks, AI ethics and explicit AI/business applications. Those changes make computational data science and predictive modelling, rather than the broad economics-and-operations-research core, the additional organising logic.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics & finance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines mathematical, statistical and econometric training with accounting, business foundations, banking and finance, macroeconomics and behavioural economics; this supports a finance direction without overstating UCR as offering a full specialist quantitative-finance major.
alternatives.concept: A quantitative economics and finance direction combining mathematics, statistics, econometrics and programming with corporate finance, banking, macroeconomics, microeconomics and financial decision-making.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest-match curriculum, the finance route adds business foundations, database management, Money, Banking & Finance and behavioural economics while dropping advanced algorithms, logic and discrete mathematics, optimisation and reinforcement learning. Those changes shift the curricular centre toward financial and economic decision-making. It differs still more clearly from the data-science route through its accounting, banking, public-economics and behavioural-economics content.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Econometrics and Operations Research bachelor. The official programme offers four third-year majors. Econometrics most directly continues the common econometric core and is less domain-specific than Data Science for Econometrics, Quantitative Finance or Quantitative Logistics, so it is selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three target-responsive concepts pass substantive and numerical distinctness and current-course feasibility. The broad core combines actual mathematics, inference, econometrics, economics and optimisation. Data science adds software construction, databases, neural networks and AI applications/ethics; finance adds securities, banking, accounting and behavioural economic decisions. Logistics was challenged against actual algorithms/optimisation and entrepreneurship, circular-business and sustainability evidence; these do not establish a sustained distinct logistics inquiry into routing, networks, inventory, queues or supply-chain operations. This is a course-content judgment, not a missing-planning no-match. Three supported alternatives reach the maximum; careers and individual examples do not generate extras.

blocks: Both study limits, differentiation and integration. UCR adds dynamic modelling; the comparator puts more weight on formal proof and includes multivariable Lagrange methods.

Both continue calculus into advanced analysis and differential equations. UCR also covers multivariable and complex calculus; the comparator places explicit emphasis on rigorous definitions and proofs.
Both provide foundational statistical methods; UCR Research Methods & Statistics is broader and more applied than the comparator's dedicated introductory statistics course.
Both cover multivariate statistical analysis; UCR teaches it in a behavioural-science research context rather than an econometrics-specific context.
Both are introductory programming courses; UCR uses Python rather than the comparator's Java-focused implementation.

UCR studies local/global and first- and second-order optimisation, alongside search, constraints and discrete methods. This is a substantive partial relationship to nonlinear optimisation, with a broader AI setting.
Both concern advanced algorithmic solution methods for optimisation problems; UCR is broader than the comparator's dedicated combinatorial-optimisation course.

UCR studies discrete temporal probabilistic models and Markov decision processes. This is a partial relationship to stochastic-process modelling; continuous-time chains, queueing and Brownian motion remain differences.
Both develop object-oriented programming, inheritance and polymorphism. UCR uses C++ and Haskell and adds software design/testing; the comparator continues Java and its libraries.
UCR Introduction to Economics covers both micro- and macroeconomics; this row aligns it only with the comparator's introductory microeconomics component.
Both develop regression-based econometric estimation and empirical analysis; the comparator continues with additional econometrics courses beyond UCR's single dedicated course.
Both provide finance foundations and quantitative financial decision-making, though the UCR course is broader in banking and practical investment decisions.
Both develop academic writing, argumentation and presenting. UCR teaches introductory research literacy and civic engagement; the comparator trains communication of econometric work and LaTeX.

UCR supplies moral-philosophy foundations corresponding to the general ethics part. It does not cover the comparator’s specific econometric research-integrity and adviser–client knowledge-asymmetry cases.

audience.programmeDescription: Econometrics and Operations Research at Erasmus University Rotterdam combines a substantial mathematical and statistical core with programming, econometrics, economics and operations research. The reviewed 2026–2027 route adds the Econometrics major, open profiling space, ethics, career preparation and a major-linked bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes offer related study through quantitative economics and optimisation, econometrics with data science, or quantitative economics and finance. Each provides sustained mathematics, statistics, programming and economic analysis. Software construction, probabilistic decision models and numerical methods contribute defined additional skills. UCR has one dedicated econometrics course and does not reproduce the full advanced econometrics, time-series, simulation, major seminar or thesis sequence.

curriculum.limitation: The selected 2026–2027 Econometrics path includes Advanced Econometrics, Quantitative Methods for Data Science and Seminar in Forecasting. It retains 12 EC of minor space and 12 EC of electives, plus two one-credit Career Skills components. The individual thesis follows the major seminar; Ethics in Econometrics is required beforehand.

cellNotes.text: Econometrics covers regression-based estimation, testing, causal analysis and prediction in Stata. It is one dedicated course, not the comparator's multi-course econometrics and time-series sequence.
Econometrics provides the dedicated econometric core; machine learning, statistics and neural networks broaden predictive modelling but do not replace advanced econometrics or time-series analysis.
Econometrics supplies regression and inference. The finance route adds accounting, banking and investment context but does not offer the comparator's specialist Quantitative Finance major.

Optimization Methods in AI studies local/global and first- and second-order optimisation, search, constraints and discrete methods. It supplies substantive optimisation study in an AI setting, without reproducing the complete operations-research sequence.
The course analyses the business, economic, governance and ethical implications of AI. It supplies application context, not technical data-science or econometric methods.

Accounting & Corporate Finance includes financial and management accounting, financial-statement analysis and investment appraisal using discounted cash flow. It supports financial decisions but does not provide specialist financial econometrics.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations adds venture and business-planning context; it does not contribute quantitative-finance methods.

PPD develops academic writing, research literacy and presenting through literature work and a community project. It is introductory and does not reproduce econometric academic communication or the Career Skills job-market programme.

notes.text: UCR does not reproduce the complete advanced econometrics, time-series analysis, mathematical economics, simulation, forecasting seminar or major-linked thesis sequence. The three programmes provide related quantitative study with these disciplinary differences.
